UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R I.A. No.202442/2023  Cashless Treatment during Golden Hour

Even as of today, the Government of India has not complied with the directions contained in order dated 8 th January, 2025 to make a Scheme in terms of sub-section 2 of Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act. 1988.
The time granted to the Government had expired on 14th March, 2025.
According to us, this is not only a very serious breach and violation of orders of this court but it is also a case of failure to implement a very beneficial provision in the statute.
List on 28th April, 2025.
We direct the Secretary of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) to personally remain present through video conference and explain the default on the part of the Central Government.

sentences.text: Firstly, we are considering the issue of directions issued to General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) regarding processing of the claims.
The order dated 8th January, 2025 records that as of 31st July, 2024, 921 claims are pending.
We direct GIC to place on record the latest figures of pending applications.
During last two months 389 claims have been settled and 583 claims are pending.
Learned Amicus Curiae has sought directions in terms of paragraphs (a) to (c) of clause 2.3 of his note filed on 24 th March, 2025.

clauses a to c read thus:
(a) GIC may appoint a Nodal Officer in each State capital to coordinate with the State authorities for expeditious submissions of the documents for all Hit and Run cases.

(b) The Chief Secretary may issue instructions to all District Magistrate/Claim Settlement Officers in the State to coordinate with the Nodal Officer appointed by GIC so that there is no delay in submission of documents and processing of claims.

(c) Details of the 523 pending claims may be provided by the GIC to the Nodal Officer of each State who may be directed to follow up with the respective District Magistrate(s) for processing of the documents and payment compensation to the victim(s).
We agree with learned Amicus Curiae and we issue directions in terms of clauses (a) to (c).
We direct the Chief Secretary of the Transport Department to issue instructions in writing to all the District Magistrates to upload the claims of hit and run cases on the GIC Portal.
Obviously, if there is a difficulty in uploading the claims or in the working of the portal, the District Magistrates are free to bring the same to the notice of GIC.

Learned Amicus pointed out that in terms of order of this Court dated 12th January, 2024, some of the State Legal Services Authorities have been diligently holding meetings regarding processing of the claims.
We direct the State Legal Services Authorities to submit reports about the compliances made by them to the office of the learned Amicus Curiae by 15th July, 2025.
We direct GIC to file an affidavit in terms of this order setting out the details of the claims processed by the same date.
Electronic Monitoring

As regards I.A. No.33035/2021,
learned Amicus Curiae has brought to our notice the steps taken by the Road Safety Committee appointed by this Court.

As far as the implementation of Section 136A of the Motors Vehicles Act,
1988, is concerned, the Road Safety Committee is dealing with the entire issue.
If the Road Safety Committee needs any directions, it can always submit a note to the learned Amicus Curiae which can be placed before this Court for furnishing necessary directions.

As far as I.A.
No.26710/2025, a date will be separately fixed for hearing of that application.

In the meanwhile,
Union of India can file affidavit by 15th July 2025 for dealing with the issues raised in this I.A. I.A.
No.77921/2024  Speed Governors

In paragraph 5.2 of the note submitted by learned Amicus Curiae, it is mentioned that the Union of India has issued advisories to the States regarding integration of retro-fitted Speed Limitation Devices (SLD) Speed Governor Data on Transport Vehicles with the Vahan-database.
We direct the Union of India to call for the reports from the State Governments regarding steps taken on the basis of advisories issued on 17th February, 2018 and 10th October, 2018.
We direct the Union of India to file a comprehensive affidavit placing on record the actions taken by the State Government by the end of July, 2025.
As regards I.A.No.76249/2024, we are informed that Union of India has filed a counter which will be considered on 28th April, 2025.
I.A. No.68786/2025  (Cashless Treatment) The prayers in this I.A. will be considered on 28th April, 2025.

If Mr. K.C. Jain, learned Advocate wants to invite attention of this Court to non-compliance with any of the directions issued by this Court, he will submit a report to that effect to learned Amicus Curiae so that this Court can fix dates for considering those non-compliances.
